decisions: alexei-led/ccgram rejected at sighting 3 rather than listed, resolving the Herdr-specificity question the 2026-08-29 audit deferred to this point. decisions: Sightings not advanced and nothing promoted, because this run fell 4 days after the 2026-09-08 audit. AGENTS.md specifies a three-week probation and the skill says nothing reaches the list in under three weeks; sightings are weekly checkpoints, not per-run counters — the three runs dated 2026-08-12 are the in-ledger precedent, and none of them advanced anything. Advancing would have taken all 14 entries first seen 2026-08-29 to sighting 3 and into the README 14 days after first sight, 11 days after the previous batch of 11 listings, pushing Extras and Phone and mobile past the soft cap. Rejected alternative: treat each run as a sighting. The cost of holding is a few days; the 2026-08-29 cohort reaches three weeks on 2026-09-19 and the 2026-09-08 cohort on 2026-09-29. Note for the next scheduled run on 2026-09-14: that is still under three weeks for the 2026-08-29 cohort, so the same reasoning holds there.

AltanS/collie kept listed despite now supporting tmux and zellij as well as Herdr — the same pattern that got alexei-led/ccgram rejected at sighting 3 on 2026-09-08. The difference is asymmetry: ccgram names Herdr as one of three interchangeable backends, while Collie's README states 'Herdr is the primary supported target in 1.0' and calls tmux and zellij experimental, tested by a single operator on one machine; its description and topics still say Herdr. It has not fallen below the bar, so per Phase 1 this is CHANGED, not probation. Rejected alternative: probation for specificity, which would treat an experimental side-backend as a change of purpose. Re-check every audit: if tmux or zellij leave experimental, it fails the same test ccgram failed.

missuo/herdrm re-promoted from rejected to candidate at sighting 1 after adopting PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 on 2026-09-10, following the 2026-08-29 precedent for pi-bellwether and herdr-nvim. The documented bar requires a license, not an open-source one, so it qualifies as written. But noncommercial terms forbid most at-work use, and that is a policy question this audit should not settle alone: flagged for human confirmation before it could reach sighting 3 (earliest 2026-10-03), and any eventual entry must say 'noncommercial use only' the way whip flags AGPL. Rejected alternative: keep it rejected as an incompatible license — the bar does not define incompatible, and inventing that rule mid-audit would be the kind of silent policy change the protocol exists to prevent.

trending.text: v0.9.1: `herdr --machine <label-or-id>` runs agent, pane, workspace, and worktree commands against a saved SSH machine without an open Herdr window (both machines need the update; failed remote commands never fall back to Local); Windows SSH hosts reachable from any platform; Letta Code detection and restore; editable text inputs; and SSH bandwidth, idle-CPU, and reconnect fixes. Supersedes the v0.9.0 release item; the v0.9.0 breaking-change item stays on its own window.

Herdr raised a $6M seed led by Bessemer Venture Partners, with Y Combinator, e2vc, and angels including Tobi Lütke (Shopify), Dane Knecht (Cloudflare), and Görkem Yurtseven (fal). The runtime stays open, the money goes to hiring, and applications go through an SSH endpoint instead of a web form. Supersedes the 2026-08-06 Y Combinator item.

v0.9.0 removes the single-process `--no-session` mode: every TUI launch now attaches to a background server, and `server stop` is what ends a session. Closing a primary workspace that has open worktree workspaces now needs explicit group intent (`workspace close --group`), and new lifecycle event subscriptions start with live events instead of replaying retained history — API and plugin clients must subscribe before taking their initial snapshot or they will miss changes.
Blog: 'Connecting the machines' — the 0.9 multi-machine client, why it took longer than expected, and Herdr Cloud named as what comes next.

v0.8.2: Windows support is now generally available on stable (previously preview-only); the plugin marketplace now discovers manifests at repository roots and subdirectories and groups multiple plugins per repository; Qwen Code state detection and native session restore.

Omarchy 4.0 'Quattro', DHH's Arch-based Linux distribution (42.6k stars), ships Herdr alongside tmux with matching keybindings and configuration, `SUPER + CTRL + RETURN` to open it, a keybindings viewer, and `hdl`/`hds`/`hdlm`/`hsl` development-layout helpers. DHH also contributed window-title sync, in-place tab moves, one-keystroke pane resizing, and outer-border control to Herdr 0.8.2. A distribution shipping it, not a company documenting production use, so the standing gap stays open.

40,215 stars on 2026-09-22, up from 38,297 on 2026-09-14 and ~15k in early July, when it hit #1 on GitHub Trending; the 'Connecting the machines' post puts downloads above 700,000. The plugin marketplace held 1,313 repositories on the same date, up from 1,144; 73 of them clear this list's 25-star bar, up from 66.
No company publicly documented as running Herdr in production could be found. Standing search target.
